audience: Infrastructure operators who need one place to admit machines, control mutations, observe health, pause work, recover state, and account for cost across a growing AI compute fleet.
problem: AI compute fleets grow as disconnected local workstations, long-lived servers, cloud VMs, provider consoles, scripts, queues, artifact stores, and billing dashboards, so expensive capacity ends up difficult to schedule, difficult to recover, and dangerous to automate.
promise: Stado Is the AI DevOps and Infrastructure Hire You Needed.

secondaryAction.label: Read the CLI reference
secondaryAction.purpose: Lower-commitment product explanation: the exact command families, arguments, and exit semantics before any install.

approvedClaims.claim: Stado is a harness for managing compute and storage across local, GCP, AWS, and Azure infrastructure.
approvedClaims.evidence: README.md#Stado: The Easiest Harness for Managing Compute and Storage Across Local, GCP, AWS, and Azure Infrastructure

approvedClaims.claim: Describe the workload, required capacity, deadline, data, and budget; Stado decides where and when to run it, then records what happened.
Stado replaces ad hoc orchestration with a provider-neutral product contract: one queue, one job lifecycle, and one result contract.
Leases, fencing, and compare-and-swap revisions prevent two workers or coordinators from owning the same transition.
approvedClaims.evidence: README.md#Share one queue across a fleet

approvedClaims.claim: Pause and drain are durable control state, not a best-effort process signal on one machine, so maintenance never deletes queued work.
Storage migration previews and executes a fenced copy, verifies names, metadata, and bodies, never allows two active writers, and never silently treats an unavailable backend as an empty queue.

A worker resolves immutable inputs, executes the workload, and publishes output plus SHA-256 evidence; secret plaintext is materialized only inside the trusted workload process and is excluded from durable job JSON.
approvedClaims.evidence: README.md#Run with reproducible inputs and bounded secrets

approvedClaims.claim: Automation and AI agents use versioned `stado machine` JSON for authorized mutations or read-only `stado-mcp` for inspection; neither interface provides unrestricted shell access or cloud-administrator credentials.
The local quick start requires no cloud account, cloud credential, Skarbiec, GPU, or Python.
`stado capabilities --json` is the source of truth for the installed build, and an implementation status does not promote an integration to stable.
Stado 0.5 is in release-candidate validation, and stable 0.5 support is intentionally limited to the local execution and local filesystem contracts.
Every cloud adapter remains preview until its own release-scoped live acceptance matrix passes; missing evidence is not promoted to stable support.
Stado is not a general Kubernetes replacement or a container platform, and it does not manage arbitrary networks, load balancers, registries, or application platforms.
Stado does not promise identical capabilities for every provider, and it does not provision physical machines or install their operating systems, GPU drivers, or workload runtimes.

requiredProof: A real terminal transcript of the minimal local configuration: `stado config init` then `stado config validate`, printing `~/.stado/config.json` and `config ok (~/.stado/config.json)`.

A real terminal transcript of the local job path: `stado local-control-plane`, then `stado submit "printf 'hello from Stado\n'"`, `stado status JOB_ID`, and `stado results JOB_ID ./results` reaching `completed` with result evidence on disk.

The documented human CLI command families printed as real command text: `stado submit|status|results|cancel`, `stado queue pause|status|drain|resume`, `stado storage ls|stat|copy|verify`, `stado doctor`, and `stado capabilities --json`.

The capability status vocabulary as `stado capabilities --json` reports it — `implemented`, `partial`, `external`, `planned`, `unsupported` — with the statement that implementation status does not mean stable support.
The supported environments matrix: macOS arm64 and Linux amd64 as supported candidates with a stable local scope, Linux arm64 not yet supported, and cloud adapters preview.

rules: Type comes from the three families in wisent-components/tokens.json: `font.expanded` ('Hubot Sans Expanded') for display headings, `font.sans` ('Hubot Sans') for body and UI, `font.mono` ('IBM Plex Mono') for every command, transcript, and code artifact. No fourth family.
One dominant foreground/background relationship: `color.background` #f8fdfb behind `color.ink` #2d3130 body copy, with `color.canvasMuted` #ecf2f0 as the only alternating section band.
Headings and deep surfaces use `color.forest` / `color.brand900` #273329; supporting copy uses `color.secondaryText` #59605d and `color.mutedText` #8b9290.

The accent role is restrained and reserved for the single primary action: `color.brand` / `color.brand500` #9ecca0 with `color.brandHover` #8dbb8f, and `color.brandLink` #769978 for inline links. Tints `color.brand50` #f9fff9 through `color.brand400` #bae6bd are for quiet surfaces only, never for large filled blocks.
Rules, card edges, and table borders use `color.border` #dee4e2 and `color.borderStrong` #c1c8c6; `color.subtleBorder` #eeeeee for the lightest dividers.

`color.success` #15803d, `color.warning` #b45309, and `color.danger` #b91c1c are reserved for real product status — for example `implemented` versus `preview` versus `unsupported` — never for decoration.
Spacing and section rhythm use the `space` scale (2px through 40px); corners use the `radius` scale (6px through 22px); depth uses `shadow.surface` and `shadow.raised` only.
Motion stays inside `motion.fast` 150ms and `motion.standard` 180ms, must explain state, sequence, or causality, and must respect reduced-motion preferences.
Use the canonical banner from this repository as the brand image; the terminal evidence is real captured output rendered in `font.mono`, never a drawn window.
forbidden: Interchangeable AI gradients, floating glass cards, excessive rounded rectangles, and decorative grids.
Fake terminal chrome or any drawn, dressed-up, or retyped terminal that is not real captured Stado output.
Motion that does not explain state, sequence, or causality.
Inventing a new logo, font, palette, or claim because a canonical asset is inconvenient to locate.
Copying another company's copy, layout, illustration, product UI, or brand assets.
Invented social proof or performance numbers: no customer names, no adoption counts, no throughput, cost-saving, or uptime figures.
Generic slogans that omit the product or the outcome.
Placeholder product screenshots presented as real.
Publishing before the CTA destination and analytics ownership are known.
Treating a visual-model score as proof of functional correctness.

notes: primaryAction.kind is url, so target is the approved absolute URL: the onboarding path the README links from its Quick start section. Stado publishes no signup or hosted account flow, so no signup URL may be used.
Preview status is load-bearing copy, not a caveat to hide: any cloud provider named on the page must be labelled preview until its release-scoped live acceptance evidence is recorded.
Provider status printed by the installed build is authoritative; the page must not restate capability status as if it were fixed.
Build and deploy settings for the generated site live in landing.config.json, never in this brief.
